candidate_profile.description: The candidate correctly identifies that profitability is declining because the business is selling more in open states, which are more expensive to serve, but the synthesis and prioritization are solid rather than exceptional.
behaviour_rules: Quickly note that stable product mix and similar pricing make those less likely root causes.
Use a workable framework that considers product, pricing, cost, and channel mix.
Identify distribution costs as the only major cost line that has worsened.
Recognize that open states require expensive shelf space, trade promotions, and more frequent deliveries.
Explain that regulated states are cheaper to serve because there are fewer outlets and more centralized distribution.
Conclude that a growing share of volume is shifting toward open states while regulated-state sales are declining.
Recommend analyzing profitability by state or channel and improving open-state economics, though the recommendation may remain somewhat concise.

expected_issues: Gets to the right answer, but may not synthesize the channel-mix logic especially sharply.
Recommendation may be right but somewhat light on concrete operational levers in open states.
Could more clearly emphasize that growth itself is not the issue, but where the growth is occurring.
expected_feedback_points: Good diagnosis of rising distribution costs and the open-state channel economics.
Good elimination of product mix and pricing as the main drivers.
Correct conclusion that the channel mix is shifting toward less profitable states.
Reasonable recommendation to analyze state profitability and address open-state cost drivers.
